metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [11. Dezember 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.73

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [11. Dezember 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.73
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.73
- Datum: 11.12.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
11. XII. Dear Hannah, we have today a card of my sister in law who
was visiting Eva - I must admit that she takes it seriously and is
already affected with all the responsibility-complex of the Zweigs.
In this case it is very good and you can rely upon her better than
on others. Dont worry if there come no letters regularly; we also got
~~yours~~ with a long delay. - We do not know exactly when to go and
How, firstly we want to {combine} it with a trip to Bahia and
the Northern Brazil, which would pay us half the fare and the
fares for the enormous distances are frightfully high. The disa-
greeable thing is that you have to book three weeks before as there
are few planes and we have {no} ship from the North of Brazil
on the other hand I want to finish first a little book on Brazil,
which will be very helpful to us and perhaps to others in the
future. We are now in plain summer, but I find the heat still
tolerable, only you want more sleep and eat less, what is per-
haps an advantage for my {counterpoint}. Now to you. I implore you
again and again, write freely and without scruples of all
I have, help your family and also your brother as I believe
that there is very little chance to get him now a visa. I have al-
ways tried my best {for others} and I hope, that Catas daughter will now see
in Cuba for Eismann after the death of her father - Here we
are in a particular situation because we have here the personal
responsibility for any person we would try to get over and we
know how small the chances are for a newcomer. As to Victor
I wrote him but has no reply, give Kocher and all others my
kindest regards, we must try for Hermann Neisse all immediately
in the States. In no case we shall stay in Newyork, I have to work
and could not have a quiet life there - probably we go somewhere
to a small university or near town {to be} that we could come from time
to time. All is so very obscure in those times - as to you I repeat,
do not worry about the material side of things and try to keep yourself
[Randnotiz links:] P.S. I hope you will stay the whole Christmas time in Bath and [?] Stanford
and you would not return to London but after a good rest. Yours Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf gelbem Papier. Die Randnotiz ist vertikal am linken Rand geschrieben. Die Tinte ist violett.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Kursivschrift. Einige wenige Wörter am Rand oder bei Durchstreichungen sind durch den Kontext eindeutig identifizierbar.
